dedupe_keys.name: maps of household scale livestock ownership prevalence by animal taxon in low and middle income countries university of virginia

description: Geostatistical maps of the share of households that keep poultry, swine or ruminants across low- and middle-income countries. The Dryad record says livestock ownership microdata from population-based survey programmes covering most of these countries were georeferenced, matched to time-fixed environmental and demographic covariates, and modelled to map prevalence at high resolution, motivated by zoonotic infection risk. It was first released on 14 October 2025 and is at version 7, updated on 10 August 2026, by Josh Colston, Bin Fang, Margaret N. Kosek and co-authors (University of Virginia), with files of about 87 MB in total, free under CC0 1.0. The exact grid resolution and file formats are not stated on the page read. Caveats: estimates are modelled from surveys of different years and designs, and uncertainty should be taken from the outputs. For simulation it gives the spatial spread of smallholder livestock keeping, to estimate exposure of household herds to drought, floods and animal disease outbreaks and the dependence of rural livelihoods on livestock. Related catalogue records include FAO Gridded Livestock of the World and the global livestock distribution dataset for 2000 to 2022.
